summary: Vietnam has officially signed the Artemis Accords, expanding international cooperation on lunar exploration as NASA reaches a key hardware milestone by integrating the Artemis III Space Launch System core stage with its boosters at Kennedy Space Center. On the defense front, a new Defense Intelligence Agency report indicates China has tripled its satellite fleet since 2018 and continues to develop on-orbit space weapons, coinciding with the U.S. military releasing new imagery of China's secretive space plane. To strengthen space capabilities, the Pentagon plans to provide a $150 million loan to startup Stoke Space for launch pad construction, while Shield Space launched a Space Superiority Coalition in the United Kingdom. In commercial developments, Virgin Galactic is preparing to reveal Apeiron, its first Delta-class space plane, and Rendezvous Robotics raised $20 million to build self-assembling spacecraft. Scientific achievements include the Vera C. Rubin Observatory discovering its first dwarf planet candidate beyond Neptune, researchers mapping the Sun’s outer magnetic field in 3D for the first time, and NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope capturing imagery of a turbulent star nursery. Looking ahead, readers should watch for an astronaut aboard the International Space Station to conduct Canada's first spacewalk in seven years on October 29.
